$schema_note: User-visible product improvements, newest first. Feeds the pipeline's What's-new card and the homepage footer's latest-improvement stamp — one source, both surfaces (the homepage must match the real site). Keep entries honest, dated, and user-phrased; trim to ~12.

entries.title: The Excel model goes deeper: an Operating Metrics tab
entries.blurb: A ninth tab carries the ratio ladder an IC actually checks year by year — expense ratio, NOI margin, DSCR, debt yield, breakeven occupancy, cash-on-cash — plus price, rent, NOI and OpEx per unit and per SF. Every cell is a live formula over the Cash Flow tab, so changing any assumption re-prices the ladder; when nothing states a unit count, the per-unit block says so instead of guessing.

entries.title: The legal read is on the sample screen — and the homepage
entries.blurb: The deal page's Regulation & benchmarks panel now shows in the homepage walkthrough and on /demo: the sample's Philadelphia jurisdiction run through the real rules engine — one verified rule on file, honestly marked dormant (it keys off an eviction filing, not a purchase), with source, as-of, and the state's no-rent-control fact extracted verbatim. A tiny legal note rides under the hero card too, and new tests lock every number to the engine.

entries.title: The sample artifacts are one click from the homepage
entries.blurb: The full multi-page report joined the memo and the Excel model as a public demo download, and the homepage now hands you all three — under the hero card and on the memo tile — so the artifact buttons in the miniature summary bar have the real files behind them.

entries.title: The full report now matches the memo's design language
entries.blurb: Every page of the multi-page report picked up the redesigned memo's system: brand-ticked titles with live count pills (figures pulled, comps rated, checks aggressive), zebra-striped tables, ratings as tinted chips, and summary cards with the brand bar. The sample's extracted terms now carry their in-place / pro-forma basis, and a second CI smoke test renders the whole report to PDF bytes.

entries.title: The IC memo and the Excel model got a design overhaul
entries.blurb: The one-page memo now leads with a color-coded verdict banner, chip-style buy box, zebra ranges with a highlighted base case, deal-killer cards, and a scenario trio — and a new CI test renders it to real PDF bytes on every change. The workbook's KPI tiles are outlined and its cash-flow ladder zebra-striped, with every layout-anchored test intact.

entries.title: The homepage sample screen now mirrors the real deal page
entries.blurb: The walkthrough widget uses the deal page's own five sections — Overview, Financials, Buy box, Analyses, Documents — with the real analysis names, verdict and mandate chips, and figures computed from the sample deal through the live engine. The hero card is a faithful miniature of the real summary bar, artifact buttons and all.

entries.title: Market briefs show full bedroom rents and their provenance
entries.blurb: Where the research carries a full FY2026 row — LA's Federal-Register revision, San Francisco's housing-authority sheet, Newark's state-treasury table — the brief now lists 0BR through 3BR with a verified/sourced chip, and prints the provenance note under the figure: where the number came from, and what was rejected on the way.

entries.title: Break it yourself: the return engine, live on the homepage
entries.blurb: A new interactive band puts three levers — exit cap, rent growth, vacancy — in your hands and recomputes IRR, equity multiple, cash-on-cash, exit value and NOI on every tick, through the same deterministic engine that prices real screens. Runs entirely in your browser on the labeled sample deal; no AI in the box.

entries.title: Compare shows each deal's leverage spread
entries.blurb: The side-by-side view gains a 'Leverage vs 30-yr' row — the signed spread between each deal's going-in cap and the freshest 30-yr fixed, color-coded negative / thin / positive with the same arithmetic as the deal page, captioned with the benchmark and its as-of date.

entries.title: The price ticker carries every covered market's FY2026 rent
entries.blurb: All fourteen sourced FY2026 2BR fair-market rents now ride the dark ticker — derived from the research layer, each linking to its market brief, with the DC metro's shared figure riding once instead of four times. The proof strip's sector count is computed now too; the typed-in number had drifted.

entries.title: Every covered market now carries its FY2026 fair-market rent
entries.blurb: A sourced HUD FY2026 2BR fair-market rent now backs 17 of 18 metro entries — San Francisco straight from the housing authority's own sheet, North Jersey from the state's republication of HUD's tables, LA from the April revision in the Federal Register. Seattle stays an honest gap: the widely-quoted figure turned out to be average rent, not the FMR.

entries.title: The demo shows the leverage check; Compare names covered markets
entries.blurb: The sample screen now runs the same leverage arithmetic every real deal gets, and the side-by-side Compare view carries a covered-market row — all three deal surfaces agree on scope.
